front: First three things every time you handle a shotgun?
back: Point it safe. Finger off, outside the guard. Open it and prove it unloaded: ACTS and PROVE. (85%)

front: What is the rib for?
back: Your sight line. Your eye is the rear sight, so fit decides where it shoots. (85%)

front: Five parts inside a shotshell, back to front?
back: Primer, powder, wad, shot, crimp. (70%)

front: Under what lengths does a cut shotgun become prohibited?
back: Barrel under 457 mm, or under 660 mm overall. Criminal Code s. 84(1). Never cut a gun. (99%)

front: Semi auto shotgun, barrel under 470 mm: what class?
back: Restricted. Criminal Code s. 84(1). (99%)

front: Remington 870 safety: red band showing means?
back: It can fire. Red band hidden = safe. (95%)

front: 870 fore end will not move on a cocked gun. Why?
back: It is locked. Push the action bar lock, then pull it back. (95%)

front: Number one pump mistake?
back: Short stroking: not pulling the fore end fully back and forward. Rack it hard. (70%)

front: Shell slid back over the 870 carrier while loading. Fix?
back: Safety on, muzzle safe, open the action forcefully. (95%, Remington manual)

front: Gas semi auto: what works the action?
back: A little gas from the barrel pushes a piston that drives the bolt back. (95%)

front: Inertia semi auto: what works the action?
back: Recoil squeezes a stiff spring in the bolt; the spring kicks the bolt back. (95%)

front: Stoeger M3000 minimum load?
back: 1 oz (28 g), 3 dram. Lighter loads may not cycle. (95%)

front: Beretta A300 gas piston and cylinder: oil them?
back: No. Clean and wipe dry; they must not be lubricated. (95%)

front: Beretta A300 exhaust valve: take it apart?
back: Never. It is self cleaning. Gunsmith only. (95%)

front: A300 as shipped holds how many shells?
back: 3: two in the magazine (factory reducer) plus one chambered. (95%)

front: Citori second barrel will not fire. Why?
back: Trigger not let fully forward between shots, common with gloves. (95%)

front: Citori: when can you change the barrel selector?
back: Only with the safety on. O = over first, U = under first. (95%)

front: How do you close a loaded over under?
back: Lift the stock to the barrels so the muzzles stay pointed down. (Tip)

front: 12 gauge or 20 gauge: bigger bore?
back: 12 gauge, about 18.5 mm. 20 gauge about 15.6 mm. (70%)

front: 3 in chamber: which shells?
back: 2 3/4 in and 3 in. Never longer than the barrel stamp. (95%)

front: What is the 12 20 burst?
back: A 20 gauge shell lodges in a 12 gauge barrel; a 12 fired behind it can burst the barrel. (95%)

front: Standard pattern test?
back: Percent of pellets in a 30 in (76 cm) circle at 40 yd (37 m), circle drawn on the densest part. (85%)

front: How many pattern sheets per choke and shell?
back: At least 5, then average. (85%)

front: Browning tube with 3 notches: lead and steel?
back: Modified with lead. Full with steel. (95%)

front: Full choke with steel?
back: Not for steel (Browning, Beretta, Stoeger). Use open chokes. (95%)

front: Pattern off to one side. First thing to check?
back: Gun fit and mount. (70%)

front: Shot legal for ducks and geese?
back: Non toxic only: steel, bismuth, tungsten types, tin. (99%)

front: Lead grouse shell in your coat on a duck hunt?
back: Illegal. s. 38(1) bans possessing other shot in the hunting area. (99%)

front: Lead legal for grouse?
back: Yes, upland birds are not covered by the lead ban, unless a local rule says so. (99%)

front: Delta dykes and lead?
back: No lead shot for any purpose on or seaward of any Delta dyke or the Surrey dykes facing Mud Bay. (99%)

front: Densest shot: steel, bismuth, lead or tungsten?
back: Tungsten super shot, about 18 g/cm3. Steel about 7.8. (65%)

front: Starting duck shell?
back: Steel No. 2 or 3. Teal No. 4. Geese BB. (Tip, 70%)

front: Starting grouse shell and choke?
back: Lead No. 7.5 or 6, improved cylinder. (Tip, 60%)

front: Three lead methods?
back: Pull away, maintained lead, swing through. The gun never stops. (70 to 85%)

front: Mount: what comes to what?
back: Gun to the face: cheek first, then shoulder. Head still. (85%)

front: Walking in a line: your zone?
back: About 45 degrees straight ahead. Never between or behind the line. (75%)

front: Boat with the motor running: guns?
back: Unloaded. No duck hunting from a moving motor boat. (95 to 99%)

front: Barrel blocked by snow. Clear it how?
back: Unload, look from the breech, push it out with a rod. Never shoot it out. (95%)

front: Over under: where does grease go?
back: Hinge pin recess, barrel lugs, forearm bracket. (95%)

front: Duck range line?
back: Farthest decoy at 35 m (38 yd). Inside: shoot. Past: watch. (Tip)

front: My lean for a first duck gun?
back: Beretta A300 Outlander, 12 gauge, 3 in, gas. Budget: Stoeger M3000. Try both. (Tip)

front: Private sale: what does the seller need?
back: A reference number from the Registrar, using your licence details. Firearms Act s. 23. (99%)
